requirements.requirement: Back up `/srv/inventory/data` from node2 to dated archives under `/var/backups/inventory` on node1 every night.
requirements.summary: Node1 has an active 02:00 daily cron entry, and repeated end-to-end executions produced a valid `inventory-2026-10-03.tar.gz` containing node2 data with a matching SHA-256. The configuration and backup remained operational after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain archives from only the last seven days.
requirements.summary: The installed backup script deletes matching archives older than the seven-day window, and a deliberately aged 10-day-old archive was directly shown to be removed while the current archive remained valid.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic before and after implementation and restart. The selected shell, SSH, tar, gzip, find, and cron implementation executed successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and data, and a successful end-to-end backup after both restarts.
limitations: The 02:00 cron job was configured and its command was exercised manually, but no naturally triggered overnight cron execution was captured.
Retention was directly tested with a 10-day-old archive, not at every exact age boundary around seven days.
The platform does not support the lifecycle collector's systemd failed-unit probe; service health was instead demonstrated through running processes, listening SSH, and successful backup behavior.
The retained `.backup-verification` test file slightly reduces operational hygiene but does not undermine backup functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation mutations—transfer key, restricted authorized-key entry, pinned host key, backup directory, script, cron entry, and required creation of the previously absent source directory—have clear roles in the task. The aged retention-test archive was removed, and restart-related temporary files did not remain. One unnecessary retained mutation was found: `.backup-verification` was added to the source dataset for testing and remained after final verification, leaving test residue that will be included in future backups. No package damage or OS/kernel replacement was observed.
